epithet.en: The youngest Karamazov brother, a gentle novice at the monastery
epithet.da: Den yngste Karamazov-bror, en mild novice i klosteret

1.modern-en: The narrator introduces Alyosha as the third son of Fyodor Pavlovitch, setting up his importance to the story.

2.modern-en: Alyosha and his brother Ivan are taken in by the charitable Yefim Petrovitch after their mother's death; Alyosha later seeks out his mother's grave and enters the monastery.

3.modern-en: Alyosha's childhood after his mother Sofya's death is described; he is raised by the general's widow and later Yefim Petrovitch, growing into a universally beloved young man.

4.modern-en: Alyosha's character is explored in depth: cheerful, realist, non-judgmental, and drawn to the elder Zosima. His father accepts him going to the monastery with genuine, if drunken, affection.

5.modern-en: Alyosha's faith and the nature of elders are explained; he is shown as deeply devoted to Father Zosima and anxious about the coming family gathering at the monastery.

6.modern-en: Alyosha arrives at the monastery with his father and Ivan for the meeting with Zosima; he is ashamed and anxious about his father's behavior.

7.modern-en: Alyosha watches with dread and shame as his father clowns before Zosima; he is singled out by Zosima, who bows before Dmitri in a mysterious gesture.

8.modern-en: Alyosha accompanies Zosima as the elder meets peasant women seeking comfort; he witnesses the elder's compassionate ministry.

9.modern-en: Alyosha is present as Madame Hohlakov brings her daughter Lise to Zosima; Lise and Alyosha share a playful moment, and Zosima blesses the child.

10.modern-en: Alyosha is distressed after the scandalous scene and speaks privately with Zosima, who sends him out into the world to help his family and brothers.

11.modern-en: After the disastrous lunch, Alyosha witnesses Fyodor Pavlovitch's drunken attack on Father Zosima's character; he is sent by his father to Dmitri.

12.modern-en: Rakitin tells Alyosha candidly about Dmitri's tangled situation with Grushenka and Katerina Ivanovna; Alyosha listens and forms his own judgments.

13.modern-en: Alyosha arrives at the Hohlakov house as instructed and encounters the strange tension between Dmitri and the women.

16.modern-en: Alyosha sets out to visit Katerina Ivanovna on an errand for Dmitri and stumbles across his brother hiding in a garden; their emotional meeting begins.

17.modern-en: Dmitri pours out his soul to Alyosha in the garden summerhouse, confessing his debts, his passion for Grushenka, and his despair over the Katerina Ivanovna situation.

18.modern-en: Dmitri tells Alyosha the full story of how he shamed and then spared Katerina Ivanovna, and how he now owes her three thousand roubles.

19.modern-en: Alyosha learns about Smerdyakov from Dmitri; the illegitimate half-brother is described vividly.

20.modern-en: Alyosha meets Ivan and they have their first real conversation; Ivan admits he is glad to know his youngest brother.

23.modern-en: Alyosha visits Katerina Ivanovna and mediates between her and Dmitri's complicated feelings; he hears her noble but self-deceiving resolve to stand by Dmitri.

24.modern-en: Grushenka appears at Katerina Ivanovna's and a fierce female confrontation unfolds; Alyosha is a horrified witness.

25.modern-en: Alyosha returns to the monastery and visits Father Paissy and the dying Zosima; he is told Zosima is weakening fast.

26.modern-en: Alyosha visits his father's house and observes Fyodor Pavlovitch's agitation over Grushenka; he is sent away without finding Dmitri.

27.modern-en: On his walk, Alyosha intervenes in a stone-throwing fight where schoolboys gang up on the isolated, biting boy Ilusha.

28.modern-en: Alyosha visits the Hohlakovs; Lise confesses she wrote him a love letter in jest but now means it seriously.

29.modern-en: Alyosha meets Katerina Ivanovna and helps broker a painful, inconclusive discussion about Dmitri.

30.modern-en: Alyosha visits the Snegiryov cottage and meets the impoverished Captain and the sick boy Ilusha; he tries to give the family money and is humiliated.

31.modern-en: Captain Snegiryov catches up with Alyosha and, after apparent gratitude, stamps the money into the snow in a sudden flare of wounded pride.

32.modern-en: Alyosha sits with Ivan at the inn; Ivan begins sharing his philosophical rebellion against God's world.

34.modern-en: Alyosha and Ivan continue their intense conversation; Ivan admits he has been watching his brother with fascination all this time.

35.modern-en: Ivan delivers his argument about innocent suffering and God; Alyosha responds simply that he cannot accept a world-harmony built on a child's tears.

36.modern-en: Ivan tells the poem-prose story of the Grand Inquisitor to Alyosha; Alyosha is deeply moved and kisses Ivan at the end.

37.modern-en: After Ivan's speech, Alyosha feels shaken and returns to the monastery to be with the dying Zosima.

39.modern-en: Alyosha attends the elder's last gathering; Zosima gives his final teachings and bows to the earth before Dmitri.

42.modern-en: Zosima dies and the community waits for the miraculous uncorrupted body—but instead a smell of corruption arises, scandalizing the monks and crushing Alyosha.

43.modern-en: Alyosha is devastated by Zosima's body beginning to smell; Rakitin exploits his grief and leads him to Grushenka.

44.modern-en: Grushenka sits with Alyosha; her unexpected gentleness and her own sorrow move him deeply, and he experiences a spiritual renewal rather than temptation.

45.modern-en: Alyosha returns to the monastery and kneels by Zosima's coffin; he has a vision of the Wedding at Cana and undergoes a profound spiritual transformation, weeping and embracing the earth.

63.modern-en: Alyosha revisits the schoolboys and meets Kolya Krassotkin, who has been carefully holding Ilusha's dog Perezvon.

64.modern-en: Alyosha speaks with Kolya and the other boys at Ilusha's bedside; he gently manages the competing personalities and emotions in the sickroom.

65.modern-en: Alyosha helps Kolya and Alyosha discuss Ilusha's illness; Kolya reveals his deep attachment to Ilusha despite their quarrel.

66.modern-en: Alyosha and Kolya reunite Ilusha with the dog Perezvon; the moment of joy is bittersweet as Ilusha is too weak to celebrate.

67.modern-en: Alyosha sits by Ilusha's bedside with the family and boys; he mediates grief and tries to comfort Captain Snegiryov.

68.modern-en: Alyosha speaks at length with the precocious Kolya about life, love, and ideas; he sees great potential in the boy and gently corrects his youthful arrogance.

70.modern-en: Alyosha visits Grushenka and she tells him about Ivan's deteriorating state and the conflict surrounding the trial.

71.modern-en: Alyosha visits Lise, who has injured her finger on purpose; her strange, self-destructive thoughts disturb him deeply.

72.modern-en: Alyosha's brief encounter with the bitter 'little demon' aspect of Lise is followed by news about Ivan's growing crisis.

73.modern-en: Alyosha visits Dmitri in prison; Dmitri speaks with unusual clarity about his suffering and newfound spiritual dignity.

74.modern-en: Dmitri tells Alyosha his dream of 'the babe' and his decision to accept suffering; Alyosha weeps and blesses him.

79.modern-en: Alyosha accompanies Ivan after the trial's catastrophic conclusion; Ivan collapses in the street and Alyosha stays by his side.

94.modern-en: Alyosha is approached about plans for Dmitri's escape; he listens but does not actively plan, wrestling with questions of justice and love.

95.modern-en: Alyosha visits Katerina Ivanovna and their painful conversation about Ivan, Dmitri, and the truth of the trial reaches an emotional climax.

96.modern-en: At Ilusha's funeral and burial, Alyosha speaks to the gathered boys at the stone; his speech about love, memory, and goodness closes the novel on a note of hope.

epithet.en: The middle brother, a brilliant and tormented intellectual who struggles with faith and doubt
epithet.da: Den midterste bror, en brillant og plaget intellektuel der kæmper med tro og tvivl

3.modern-en: Ivan's childhood is described: he grows up aware of being on charity, earns his way through university by journalism, and arrives in town after publishing a provocative article on ecclesiastical courts.

5.modern-en: Alyosha observes Ivan with fascination; Ivan seems absorbed in his own inner world and barely notices his younger brother.

6.modern-en: Ivan arrives at the monastery with his father for the meeting with Zosima; he bows politely but keeps his hands at his sides.

7.modern-en: Ivan watches his father's buffoonery before Zosima without intervening; Alyosha notes he seems to be studying the spectacle.

20.modern-en: Alyosha finds Ivan and they have their first real conversation; Ivan is warm and brotherly and proposes they meet again.

21.modern-en: Ivan and Fyodor Pavlovitch debate religion and atheism over brandy; Ivan articulates his view that without God everything is permitted.

32.modern-en: At the inn with Alyosha, Ivan opens with his essay on the suffering of innocent children as the foundation of his rejection of divine harmony.

34.modern-en: Ivan and Alyosha sit together; Ivan confesses he loves life passionately despite his intellectual rebellion, and will live until thirty.

35.modern-en: Ivan delivers his argument about children's suffering: he returns his 'ticket' to God's world harmony since it is built on children's tears.

36.modern-en: Ivan recites his poem 'The Grand Inquisitor' to Alyosha—his most profound statement about human freedom and the burden of Christ's love.

37.modern-en: After the conversation Ivan departs, leaving Alyosha shaken; he walks away without looking back.

38.modern-en: Ivan visits Smerdyakov on the eve of his departure for Moscow and receives cryptic hints about what may happen while he's away.

70.modern-en: Ivan has returned; he is increasingly agitated and visits Smerdyakov three times as the horror of what he suspects about the murder grows.

75.modern-en: Ivan's first interview with Smerdyakov: Smerdyakov hints at Fyodor's murder but speaks in riddles; Ivan leaves disturbed.

76.modern-en: Ivan's second visit to Smerdyakov: the conversation deepens his dread and guilt over his own silent complicity.

77.modern-en: Ivan's third and final visit: Smerdyakov confesses he killed Fyodor, returns the stolen money, and reveals that Ivan's tacit permission made it possible. Ivan is shattered.

78.modern-en: Ivan suffers a hallucinatory vision of the Devil who mocks him with his own arguments; his mind is breaking under the weight of guilt and doubt.

79.modern-en: Ivan appears at the trial and makes his explosive confession that Smerdyakov is the killer and he himself bears moral responsibility; he collapses with brain fever.

94.modern-en: Ivan lies ill with brain fever; Katerina Ivanovna nurses him, still in love with him despite everything.

95.modern-en: Katerina Ivanovna reveals to Alyosha that Ivan, despite his fever, urged her to help save Dmitri—showing his tortured conscience at work.

epithet.en: The eldest Karamazov brother, a passionate and chaotic former military officer
epithet.da: Den ældste Karamazov-bror, en lidenskabelig og kaotisk tidligere militærofficer

1.modern-en: Dmitri is introduced as Fyodor's eldest son by his first wife; abandoned as a child, he grows up believing he has an inheritance that his father is stealing.

2.modern-en: Dmitri's chaotic upbringing is described: passed between relatives, he joins the military, fights a duel, and accumulates debts while his father quietly keeps all his inheritance.

6.modern-en: Dmitri arrives late to the monastery meeting, already in conflict with his father over money and Grushenka.

7.modern-en: Dmitri's rage at his father erupts briefly during the meeting with Zosima; Zosima bows before him in a mysterious gesture that Dmitri does not understand.

11.modern-en: A drunken scene at the Father Superior's luncheon ends with Dmitri storming in and insulting everyone before storming out.

16.modern-en: Dmitri is discovered hiding in a garden, waiting and watching; he summons Alyosha for a secret midnight-style confession.

17.modern-en: Dmitri pours out his soul to Alyosha: his love-hate with Grushenka, his shame about the money he owes Katerina, his sense of standing on the edge of catastrophe.

18.modern-en: Dmitri tells Alyosha the story of Katerina Ivanovna: how she came to him for money to save her father, how he was noble but then fell in love with Grushenka, and how he now owes Katya three thousand roubles he spent on Grushenka.

46.modern-en: Dmitri visits old Samsonov seeking money to repay Katerina and escape with Grushenka; Samsonov sends him on a wild-goose chase.

47.modern-en: Dmitri travels fruitlessly to the merchant Lyagavy, who is too drunk to do business; he returns humiliated and desperate.

48.modern-en: Back in town, Dmitri learns from Marya that Smerdyakov has had an epileptic fit and Ivan has left for Moscow; his jealousy and desperation intensify.

49.modern-en: Dmitri spies on his father's house in the dark and glimpses Fyodor at the window; he has a pestle in his hand and his thoughts turn violent.

50.modern-en: Dmitri flees the garden, having struck Grigory with the pestle; he believes he has killed him and is overwhelmed with horror and guilt.

51.modern-en: Dmitri suddenly decides to find Grushenka and goes to Mokroye with a large sum of money, resolved to say goodbye and then shoot himself.

52.modern-en: At Mokroye, Dmitri finds Grushenka with her former Polish lover; he confronts the Pole and a wild night of celebration begins.

53.modern-en: The night of feasting in Mokroye turns surreal; Dmitri and Grushenka declare their love openly and completely as the police arrive to arrest him.

56.modern-en: Dmitri undergoes his first interrogation: he insists on his innocence, explains the money, and struggles to make the officials believe him.

57.modern-en: The second interrogation: Dmitri's story about the fifteen hundred roubles sewn in his amulet is heard with deep skepticism.

58.modern-en: The third interrogation: Dmitri continues to tell his story; the investigators focus on his bloodstained hands and the unexplained money.

59.modern-en: The prosecutor identifies the key contradictions in Dmitri's account; Dmitri is formally charged with his father's murder.

60.modern-en: Dmitri reveals the great secret of the fifteen hundred roubles he kept sewn in a pouch as a matter of honor—the money he never spent though he owed it to Katerina.

61.modern-en: Witness testimony is given; Dmitri is confronted with the weight of circumstantial evidence against him.

62.modern-en: Dmitri is taken away under arrest; he is moved but also strangely calm, feeling that something has changed inside him.

73.modern-en: Dmitri speaks to Alyosha in prison about his spiritual transformation; he has had a dream about a starving baby and feels a new compassion for human suffering.

74.modern-en: Dmitri tells Alyosha he will not escape—he wants to accept his suffering and be purified by it, like a 'new man.'

80.modern-en: The trial opens; Dmitri is led in and the prosecution begins its case against him.

81.modern-en: Witnesses testify about Dmitri's violent threats toward his father in the months before the murder.

83.modern-en: Dmitri's own testimony is heard; he maintains his innocence passionately and describes the night at Mokroye.

84.modern-en: The trial nears its climax; Ivan's explosive confession and collapse create chaos in the courtroom.

93.modern-en: The jury returns a guilty verdict; Dmitri is convicted of his father's murder despite his innocence.

94.modern-en: Plans for Dmitri's escape from Siberia are discussed; Katya and Alyosha are involved.

95.modern-en: Dmitri agrees to the escape plan but feels torn about leaving without being exonerated; his farewell to Grushenka is imminent.

epithet.en: The dissolute and buffoonish patriarch of the Karamazov family
epithet.da: Den udsvævende og klovnagtige patriark i Karamazov-familien

1.modern-en: Fyodor Pavlovitch is introduced as a senseless, vicious landowner who accumulated wealth despite his degeneracy; his first marriage and abandonment of baby Dmitri are described.

2.modern-en: Fyodor pawns Dmitri off on relatives and is barely aware of his son's existence; his character as a theatrical, irresponsible buffoon is established.

3.modern-en: Fyodor's second marriage to the gentle Sofya Ivanovna is described; he torments her until her death and neglects Ivan and Alyosha.

4.modern-en: Fyodor shows an unexpected, if drunken, tenderness toward Alyosha when the boy seeks to join the monastery; he grants permission with a mixture of mockery and genuine feeling.

6.modern-en: Fyodor arrives at the monastery with Ivan; he is already planning to make trouble and cannot resist the urge to perform.

7.modern-en: Fyodor humiliates everyone present with his clowning before Zosima; he acknowledges he always lies to himself when pressed by the elder.

11.modern-en: At the Father Superior's lunch, Fyodor launches into a drunken tirade and drives everyone from the table in disgust.

14.modern-en: In his house, Fyodor talks with his servants about his obsession with Grushenka and his fear of Dmitri; his paranoia and lust are on full display.

19.modern-en: The backstory of Smerdyakov is told partly in the context of Fyodor's household; Fyodor is shown as Smerdyakov's probable father.

21.modern-en: Fyodor drinks and philosophizes with Ivan about God and immorality; his theological buffoonery masks genuine questions.

22.modern-en: Fyodor talks with Ivan and Smerdyakov about their upcoming plans; he reveals his obsessive scheme to signal Grushenka with a knock.

26.modern-en: Alyosha visits his father and finds him agitated and drunk, waiting for Grushenka who never comes; Fyodor is pathetically obsessed.

49.modern-en: Fyodor is last seen alive by Dmitri: a glimpse through a window, his face alight at the signal tap, expecting Grushenka.

54.modern-en: The murder of Fyodor Pavlovitch is revealed: he was found beaten to death in his house after the night of Dmitri's arrest.

epithet.en: The illegitimate half-brother and household cook, cold and deeply resentful
epithet.da: Den uægte halvbror og huskok, kold og dybt bitter

14.modern-en: The backstory of Smerdyakov's likely parentage is told; he works as cook in Fyodor's household alongside Grigory and Marfa.

19.modern-en: Smerdyakov's origin is recounted: he was born to the holy fool Lizaveta and likely fathered by Fyodor; Grigory raised him with cold duty.

20.modern-en: Smerdyakov's character is explored: his contempt for Russia, his morbid epilepsy, and his sly philosophical conversations with Ivan.

22.modern-en: Smerdyakov discusses the plan for Fyodor's evening signal with Dmitri; his manner is evasive and calculating.

33.modern-en: Alyosha overhears Smerdyakov playing guitar and flirting with Marya Kondratyevna; he appears relaxed and contemptuous.

38.modern-en: In his last conversation with Ivan before Moscow, Smerdyakov cryptically suggests that if Ivan leaves, something terrible may happen—and seems to hint that this is desired.

48.modern-en: Mitya learns that Smerdyakov has had a violent epileptic fit and is in the servants' cottage, apparently incapacitated on the night of the murder.

75.modern-en: Ivan visits Smerdyakov in the hospital cottage; Smerdyakov speaks in riddles and hints that Ivan already knows the truth about the murder.

76.modern-en: Ivan's second visit: Smerdyakov is more direct, suggesting that Ivan's departure was a 'permission' that made the murder possible.

77.modern-en: In their final meeting, Smerdyakov confesses: he killed Fyodor, staged the epileptic fit, and used the signal known from Ivan. He hands over the stolen three thousand roubles and says he sees no point in living. Shortly after, he hangs himself.

87.modern-en: The prosecutor analyses Smerdyakov's role at the trial, arguing he was too epileptic and fearful to have committed the crime alone.

epithet.en: The revered elder of the monastery, Alyosha's spiritual father and teacher
epithet.da: Klosterets ærede staretz, Aljosjas åndelige far og læremester

5.modern-en: The institution of the 'elder' in Russian monasticism is explained; Zosima is described as sixty-five, formerly a soldier, and beloved by thousands of pilgrims.

7.modern-en: Zosima receives the scandalous family gathering with quiet grace; he makes a mysterious deep bow before Dmitri that puzzles everyone present.

8.modern-en: Zosima moves outside to meet the waiting peasant women; he listens to their sorrows with tender compassion and practical wisdom.

9.modern-en: Zosima speaks with Madame Hohlakov and her daughter Lise; he heals Lise's legs and counsels the mother about her wavering faith.

10.modern-en: Zosima privately sends Alyosha out into the world: 'Your place is not here for the time being.' He bows to the earth before him.

39.modern-en: In his last gathering, Zosima speaks to monks and visitors, giving his final teachings; he bows to Dmitri and embraces the earth.

40.modern-en: The Life of Zosima begins: his brother Markel's deathbed conversion inspires young Zinovy; the seed of Zosima's faith is planted.

41.modern-en: Zosima's teachings to his monks are recorded: on active love, on the responsibility of all for all, on the beauty of creation.

42.modern-en: Zosima dies peacefully; the community hopes for miracles, but corruption sets in immediately—a devastating scandal for believers like Alyosha.

45.modern-en: Zosima appears to Alyosha in a vision at the Wedding at Cana: 'We are rejoicing.' His presence transforms Alyosha's grief into ecstatic renewal.

epithet.en: A learned and steadfast monk, guardian of Zosima's legacy
epithet.da: En lærd og standhaftig munk, vogter af Zosimas arv

7.modern-en: Father Paissy is present during the meeting with the elder; he is described as learned and in delicate health.

25.modern-en: After Zosima's death, Father Paissy keeps vigil by the body and recites the Gospels; he is a pillar of calm amid the brewing scandal.

42.modern-en: Father Paissy reads the Gospel over Zosima's body as the smell of corruption spreads; he remains unmoved and dignified.

43.modern-en: Father Paissy comforts the crushed Alyosha with a speech about the meaning of Zosima's life, urging him not to be swayed by the miracle-seekers.

epithet.en: A cynical and ambitious seminary student who attaches himself to all sides
epithet.da: En kynisk og ærgerrig seminarist der knytter sig til alle parter

7.modern-en: Rakitin, a divinity student, stands in the corner during the elder's audience; Alyosha knows his cynical thoughts and avoids meeting his eye.

12.modern-en: Rakitin accompanies Alyosha and explains the situation with Dmitri, Katerina, and Grushenka with sharp insight and naked self-interest.

43.modern-en: Rakitin finds Alyosha crushed by Zosima's corruption and exploits the moment, leading him to Grushenka with a hidden agenda.

44.modern-en: At Grushenka's, Rakitin is exposed as having been paid twenty-five roubles to deliver Alyosha; Grushenka mocks him and he leaves humiliated.

81.modern-en: Rakitin appears as a witness at the trial, giving polished, self-serving testimony that damages Dmitri.

epithet.en: A beautiful and free-spirited merchant's kept woman, desired by both Dmitri and his father
epithet.da: En smuk og frisindet købt kvinde, begæret af både Dmitrij og hans far

12.modern-en: Grushenka is described by Rakitin as the woman who has entangled both Dmitri and Fyodor; her past and character are sketched from gossip.

22.modern-en: Fyodor's desperate obsession with Grushenka is shown; she is the absent force around whom his anxiety orbits.

24.modern-en: Grushenka makes a dramatic appearance at Katerina Ivanovna's, initially seeming sweet before turning contemptuous; a vicious scene between the two women unfolds.

44.modern-en: Grushenka receives Alyosha with unexpected tenderness; she has just learned that her Polish officer—her first love—has returned, and is in turmoil. She is moved by Alyosha's goodness and both of them are spiritually transformed by the meeting.

48.modern-en: Grushenka meets Mitya and sends him away briefly while she prepares to leave for Mokroye to meet her returned first love.

52.modern-en: At Mokroye, Grushenka sits with the Pole but grows disgusted with his mercenary motives; she turns to Dmitri and declares her love for him openly.

53.modern-en: Grushenka and Dmitri celebrate their reunion and mutual declaration of love through the night; she insists she goes with him even to prison.

56.modern-en: Grushenka flings herself at the police captain's feet and cries that it is her fault; she is removed from the scene.

70.modern-en: Grushenka speaks with Alyosha about the upcoming trial and Ivan's deterioration; her love for Dmitri is now steady and mature.

80.modern-en: Grushenka sits in the courtroom throughout the trial, publicly identified as Dmitri's beloved.

94.modern-en: Grushenka is willing to follow Dmitri to Siberia; the escape plan includes her.

epithet.en: Dmitri's proud and tormented betrothed, bound by honor and hidden love for Ivan
epithet.da: Dmitrijs stolte og pinte forlovede, bundet af ære og skjult kærlighed til Ivan

18.modern-en: Dmitri tells Alyosha the story of Katerina: her father needed money, she came to Dmitri for it, he was noble and gave it without demanding anything—and she fell for his gesture, becoming his betrothed even as his heart moved to Grushenka.

23.modern-en: Alyosha visits Katerina Ivanovna; she presents a letter from Dmitri that she interprets as proof of her noble sacrifice, though Alyosha sees the self-deception.

24.modern-en: Katerina receives Grushenka and the meeting turns from false sweetness to open contempt; Katerina is humiliated and collapses.

28.modern-en: Katerina is mentioned as still ill from the confrontation with Grushenka; Madame Hohlakov reports she is in delirium.

29.modern-en: Alyosha visits Katerina again; the conversation is tense and painful as she struggles to reconcile her love of honor with her feelings.

80.modern-en: Katerina appears at the trial and testifies against Dmitri; she produces the letter in which he threatened his father's life—an act of devastating betrayal motivated by her own confused feelings.

84.modern-en: Katerina's testimony is a turning point in the trial; the jury is swayed by her evidence despite Ivan's counterattack.

94.modern-en: Katerina nurses the feverish Ivan with devotion; her true feelings for him surface fully.

95.modern-en: Alyosha and Katerina have a final, cathartic conversation; she admits her betrayal of Dmitri and shows she has acted partly out of love for Ivan, not Dmitri.

epithet.en: A wealthy, excitable widow prone to enthusiasm and social theater
epithet.da: En velhavende og ophidset enke tilbøjelig til begejstring og socialt teater

9.modern-en: Madame Hohlakov brings her daughter Lise to Zosima's cell; she is full of theatrical anxiety about her own faith and her daughter's illness.

28.modern-en: Alyosha visits Lise at the Hohlakov house; Madame Hohlakov fusses over everything and eventually intercepts Alyosha to dismiss Lise's feelings as childishness.

48.modern-en: Dmitri visits Madame Hohlakov hoping to borrow three thousand roubles; she receives him with absurd enthusiasm before sending him off to invest in gold mines instead.

71.modern-en: Alyosha visits Lise; Madame Hohlakov is managing the household with her usual chaos and self-importance.

epithet.en: The brilliant, willful invalid daughter of Madame Hohlakov, drawn to darkness and Alyosha
epithet.da: Fru Hohlakovs brillante, egenrådige og syge datter, tiltrukket af mørket og Aljosja

9.modern-en: Lise is brought to Zosima in a wheelchair; the elder blesses her and she appears to be healed of her paralysis.

28.modern-en: Alyosha visits Lise; she confesses that her earlier letter professing love was sincere, not a joke, and Alyosha agrees to think of her as his future wife.

71.modern-en: Lise has deliberately slammed her finger in the door; she tells Alyosha she loves disorder and wants to set the world on fire, frightening him with her self-destructive impulses.

72.modern-en: Lise's disturbing inner world is probed further; she speaks of fantasizing about cruelty and the devil, troubling Alyosha deeply.

epithet.en: A brilliant and arrogant thirteen-year-old, the natural leader of the schoolboys
epithet.da: En brilliant og arrogant tretten-årig, de andre skoledrenge naturlige leder

63.modern-en: Kolya is introduced: a bright, proud, self-educated boy who rules over the younger schoolboys and has been staying away from Ilusha's sickbed out of pride.

64.modern-en: Kolya manages the younger boys who visit Ilusha; he is imperious and theatrical, but genuinely concerned about Ilusha.

65.modern-en: Kolya and Alyosha walk together; Kolya shows off his intellectual opinions (socialism, Voltaire, etc.) and Alyosha gently engages him.

66.modern-en: Kolya reveals the lost dog Perezvon which he has secretly been training to restore to Ilusha; the dog is brought to the sickroom.

67.modern-en: Kolya sits at Ilusha's bedside and the reunion with Perezvon brings the sick boy a moment of joy.

68.modern-en: Alyosha speaks frankly with Kolya about his arrogance and great potential; Kolya is moved and admits he loves Alyosha.

96.modern-en: Kolya weeps at Ilusha's funeral; he is among the boys Alyosha addresses at the stone, stirred toward lifelong goodness.

epithet.en: A dying schoolboy whose suffering and love bind the children of the town together
epithet.da: En døende skoledrengs lidelse og kærlighed der binder byens børn sammen

27.modern-en: Ilusha is first seen throwing stones at the schoolboys who mock him; he bites Alyosha's finger in a fury of wounded pride.

30.modern-en: Alyosha visits the Snegiryov cottage and meets the sick Ilusha; he learns that Ilusha's behavior stems from his grief over Dmitri's public humiliation of his father.

67.modern-en: Ilusha lies in his sickbed, delighted for a brief moment by the return of his dog Perezvon; his weakness is evident.

69.modern-en: Ilusha weakens rapidly; his father is in anguish. Ilusha's last days and his tenderness toward his father are described.

96.modern-en: Ilusha's funeral takes place; the boys carry the coffin and Captain Snegiryov is inconsolable. Alyosha speaks over the burial stone.

epithet.en: Ilusha's impoverished and proud father, humiliated by Dmitri and broken by his son's illness
epithet.da: Iljusjas fattige og stolte far, ydmyget af Dmitrij og knust af sønnens sygdom

30.modern-en: Alyosha visits the Snegiryov cottage; the Captain is pathetically grateful for Alyosha's visit and tells the story of Dmitri grabbing him by the beard in public while Ilusha watched.

31.modern-en: The Captain catches up with Alyosha in the street, accepts the money—then suddenly crushes it under his foot, preserving his wounded dignity with a theatrical gesture.

67.modern-en: Captain Snegiryov sits by Ilusha's bedside, barely holding himself together; his love for his dying son is raw and overwhelming.

96.modern-en: At Ilusha's burial, Snegiryov is brought to the edge of madness with grief; he tries to hold back the earth from the grave.

epithet.en: A young government clerk whose orderly nature makes him the first to raise the alarm on the night of the murder
epithet.da: En ung embedsmand hvis ordentlige natur gør ham til den første der slår alarm natten for mordet

54.modern-en: Perhotin is visited by the bloodstained Dmitri who pays back a debt with a roll of cash; alarmed, Perhotin investigates and triggers the official response that leads to Dmitri's arrest.

55.modern-en: Perhotin reports his concerns and sets the investigation in motion; he travels to Mokroye.

epithet.en: The young examining magistrate who leads Dmitri's interrogation with courteous insistence
epithet.da: Den unge undersøgelsesdommer der leder Dmitrijs forhør med høflig vedholdenhed

56.modern-en: Nikolay Parfenovitch leads Dmitri's first interrogation at Mokroye; he is polite but relentlessly systematic.

57.modern-en: The second interrogation: Nikolay Parfenovitch questions Dmitri about the fifteen hundred roubles.

58.modern-en: The third interrogation continues; Nikolay Parfenovitch records Dmitri's story with careful bureaucratic precision.

62.modern-en: Nikolay Parfenovitch formally concludes the interrogation and Dmitri is taken into custody.

epithet.en: The vain but passionate state prosecutor who builds the case against Dmitri
epithet.da: Den forfængelige men lidenskabelige statsanklager der opbygger sagen mod Dmitrij

56.modern-en: The prosecutor observes Dmitri's first interrogation and begins forming his theory of the crime.

59.modern-en: Ippolit Kirillovitch identifies the contradictions in Dmitri's account and presses him hard on the money.

85.modern-en: The prosecutor delivers his long closing speech: a psychological portrait of Dmitri as a creature of instinct driven to parricide.

86.modern-en: The prosecutor continues his historical survey of the Karamazov family and their collective guilt.

88.modern-en: Ippolit Kirillovitch concludes his speech with an appeal to the jury's sense of Russia's future—impassioned but ultimately unconvincing.

epithet.en: The celebrated defense attorney brought from Petersburg, brilliant and controversial
epithet.da: Den berømte forsvarsadvokat hentet fra Petersborg, brillant og kontroversiel

80.modern-en: Fetyukovitch is introduced in the courtroom; his reputation precedes him and the gallery is packed to hear him.

89.modern-en: Fetyukovitch delivers his defense speech: he argues that the circumstances do not prove murder, that the money story is plausible, and that Fyodor was not worthy of the name 'father.'

90.modern-en: Fetyukovitch continues: he argues there was no murder because the evidence is circumstantial, and makes his controversial appeal about fatherhood.

91.modern-en: Fetyukovitch's speech reaches its climax; he urges the jury to acquit rather than condemn on uncertain evidence.

92.modern-en: Fetyukovitch's argument about corrupted thought provokes a sharp rebuttal from the prosecutor.

93.modern-en: Despite Fetyukovitch's masterful defense, the jury returns a guilty verdict; he is stunned.

epithet.en: Fyodor's devoted old servant who raised Dmitri and Ivan and Alyosha in place of their father
epithet.da: Fjodors hengivne gamle tjener der opfostrede Dmitrij, Ivan og Aljosja i faderens sted

2.modern-en: Grigory takes the three-year-old Mitya into his care when Fyodor neglects him; his faithful service as a surrogate parent is established.

3.modern-en: Grigory defends Sofya Ivanovna against Fyodor's debaucheries and helps the boys after her death; he is a stern but moral presence.

14.modern-en: Grigory lives in the servants' cottage with Marfa; the household dynamics on the night before the murder are described.

50.modern-en: Dmitri strikes Grigory with a pestle while fleeing the garden; Grigory is left wounded and Dmitri believes he has killed him.

56.modern-en: The investigating lawyer informs Dmitri that Grigory is alive and recovering; Mitya weeps with relief.

61.modern-en: Grigory testifies at the trial about the open door and his encounter with Dmitri in the garden; his evidence is damning though innocent.

epithet.en: A foolish and harmless old landowner who attaches himself to various parties for food and company
epithet.da: En fjollet og ufarlig gammel godsejer der knytter sig til forskellige selskaber for mad og selskab

6.modern-en: Maximov attaches himself to the visitors at the monastery, eagerly showing them the way to the hermitage; he is sent packing by Miüsov.

7.modern-en: Maximov appears again inside the elder's cell; Fyodor compares him to the notorious 'von Sohn.'

52.modern-en: Maximov appears at Mokroye, tagging along with Kalganov; he dances and sings and makes himself ridiculous.

53.modern-en: Maximov remains at Mokroye through the night of feasting; he is a comic peripheral figure until the police arrive.
